title: Check if Bitwise OR Has Trailing Zeros
statement:
You get an array `nums` of positive integers. Decide whether you can pick at least two of its elements (at different positions) so that the bitwise OR of all picked elements ends in at least one `0` bit when written in binary, i.e. the OR is even. For instance `4` is `100` in binary and ends in two zeros, while `5` is `101` and ends in none.

Return `true` if such a choice exists and `false` if it does not.
notes:
## Intuition

OR can only switch bits on, never off. The OR has a trailing zero exactly when its lowest bit is `0`, and that bit is `0` only if every picked number has lowest bit `0`, that is, every picked number is even. Adding more numbers never helps, so it is enough to ask whether some pair works, and a pair works exactly when both numbers are even. Checking every pair (the brute force) is O(n²); counting even numbers is O(n).

## Approach

1. Set `evenCount` to 0.
2. For each `value`, test its lowest bit with `value & 1`; if it is `0`, the value is even, so increase `evenCount`.
3. As soon as `evenCount` reaches 2, those two evens form a valid pair: return `true`.
4. If the loop ends first, at most one value is even: return `false`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`. `1` is odd. `2 & 1 = 0`, so `evenCount = 1`. `3` is odd. `4 & 1 = 0`, so `evenCount = 2` and the answer is `true` (indeed `2 | 4 = 6 = 110` in binary).

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass over `nums`.
- Space: O(1): only a counter.

## Pitfalls

- A single even number is not enough: you must pick at least two elements, and any odd partner sets the lowest bit.
- Selecting more elements never helps; do not search over all subsets.
- Write `(value & 1) === 0` with parentheses: equality binds tighter than `&` in JavaScript, Java and C.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `evenCount` | how many even numbers have been seen so far |
| `value` | the current element of `nums` |

narration.2: Count the even numbers: only even numbers can be part of a valid choice.
narration.4: The lowest bit is 0 exactly when the number is even.
narration.7: Two evens are enough: their OR also has lowest bit 0.
narration.11: At most one even number exists, so every pick includes an odd number and the OR is odd.
